steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Huff...

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Why are you still here?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm going to be scuttling around here like a four-legged Metal Crab on the beach until I can get all your signatures.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Fine, scuttle on then. I'm packing up, going home and having a drink.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Be my guest.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: I bought this new gadget at the market today, this 'Originium Microwave Massager' something or other. Columbian thing. Can't make sense of it, but it works wonders. Feels like real relief sticking it on my back.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: It's not bad trying something new.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Was that shaggy beckbeast riding a surfboard on the roof one of your funnies too?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Shaggy beckbeast? No, that's not...

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Shame about that, I liked it. Entertainment that good has been rare ever since we lost the Obsidian Festival.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I'm glad it made you happy...

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Right, got something for you.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: ...A kalimba?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Did you pick this up from the same market?

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Congrats on the marriage, sonny.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: You got a safe job for your family. A boring one, but you've got a sense of responsibility.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: I can understand you like stability, but life's full of ways. Don't live out the hound days, son.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Each day lived is a hound day... you just have to roll with the punches.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: I used to gamble with your grandpa, if you'll remember. We said you'd always come back from Obsidian with the grand prize one day.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: Honestly... what a waste of all that musical talent.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: If you're interested, I can still bring my guitar out sometime. Play it for you again.

steps.name: Elderly Shopkeeper
steps.text: If you'd played us a number on that thing sooner, your letter might've been the first to have my signature on it.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Thanks.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mrs. Harley, we recovered the surfboards that went missing here. Can you check if that's all of them?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm so sorry about this...

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: You helped me here. What are you apologizing for?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: I didn't think these old things would ever get used again. It's funny—just who would've taken them?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh, well, I'm not too sure either...

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: That's alright, girl. It could be some tourists just picked them up while they were having too much fun—no harm, no foul. How are you? Did you have fun today?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: You mean getting drenched in hot spring water?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Didn't it bring back a little of that seaside fun? It hasn't been so lively in forever—even the customers here to drink were all smiles.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Those owners were always frowning day in and day out. Even the drink was starting to taste bad...
Harley looks towards the tourists outside who still haven't scattered. Sunset gradually dyes the sky. Every single person's feeling merry.

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: It's like we've gone back years and years.
A man listlessly heads for the old cafe, and pushes open its door once again.

He feels for the light switch. Carefully, he uses a rag to wipe the dust from the counter, then pulls the equipment out from the cupboards, before pulling a pouch out of his chest pocket. Fresh coffee beans, brought back from the office.
Like so many years ago, he boils, he grinds, then attentively, he pours.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Huff...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Flavor is... I guess I've gotten rusty.

He looks out of the window. One after another, people make their way home while it's still dusk. The street grows gradually more desolate, until there's no one out at all. Only then does he chuckle to himself, bitterly.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Seriously... what the hell am I waiting for?
He finishes his coffee, and prepares to tidy everything away and get out of here.
A knock comes from the door. Costa remembers he never even shut it.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Who is it?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Good evening...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Are you still open?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly, you promise you've made it clear to the Little Black Sheep? Not to cause trouble like this anymore?

spans.text: you've made it clear to the Little Black Sheep? Not to cause trouble like this anymore?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Yep... any more mess, and I'll disavow them as my clones.

steps.name: Dozy Creature
steps.text: (Tumbles about in the air)

steps.name: Agitated Creature
steps.text: (Headbutts walls in the street)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Fine, I'll try as hard as I can...

steps.name: Dozy Creature
steps.text: (Attempts to walk calmly)

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: See? Much better.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But they still caused plenty of chaos at the trade fair today...

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: But the air was full of the smell of joy, you mean. Mmm, it's sugary sweet even now. It's just like the first time I took a walk across the 'countries' you talk about.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Where there's hilly areas, you can glide. Where there's watery areas, you can surf. I even had a couple of bastard annoying animals chasing me all over the wilds. Every place produces something different.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Knowing how your human race can't just tour the whole place, getting to see such interesting things must be novel for you, right?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Why do I get the sense you're showing off, Mr. Dolly?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Busted.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Did you have fun today then, Adele? Hot springs let you relax, skateboarding's a thrill, and that loud-ass penguin's loud-ass music got you pumped up, didn't it?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly, those children could see the lambs!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: *sigh* How is it this hard to cheer you up? There's that 'brooding' flavor in the air again, bitter and tart!
Adele turns away to hide a little giggle, then recovers her straight face.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Mr. Dolly, we're here. I need to leave the owner a note saying we've found the exhibit, and thank you for worrying about us.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I have the pen and paper in my bag...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Oh, is this cafe... open again?
Dim yellow lights perfuse the interior. Through the windows, the cafe's furnishings can vaguely be made out.
Costa pours hot water, the sound breaking the silence between him and his customer.
Condensation fills the windows. Adele gently wipes the hot springs' white mist from the glass, and finally catches a proper glimpse of the customer.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: What did we stop for? Aren't we going in for coffee?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: ...Professor Keller?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I got The Atlas of Terra's Volcanoes. I never thought you'd have kept it safe for so many years... Thank you.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Ah, I asked a little lady. She came here looking for some exhibit. Just so happened to be the Volcano Museum's.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Is, um, she your employee?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele is my student.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Ah, your student. Right, right...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: You've been...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: ...quite the miserable worker at city hall lately. Gathering signatures for an LOI to relocate the residents...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: My parents left their own little clothing shop. Reasonably speaking, I should need to sign too.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Do you... have any objections to the redevelopment, then?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Our family stopped leaning on this place for our livelihood long ago. If it would make your work go any smoother...?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Of course, and thank you for your cooperation...

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Want another cup?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Can that come with the old complimentary chat, then?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: As a qualified barista, listening is part of my work.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Take a seat, then.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Maybe we should go, Mr. Dolly? Today doesn't seem like the right one to leave a message.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Aww, but the coffee smells so good. Can't we have some...?

steps.name: Agitated Creature
steps.text: (Prepares to charge headlong into the cafe)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Hey... hey!
The closed glass door blocks the lamb's strike, and it hardly makes as loud a noise as she expected. It simply turns tail and shoots back into the street, where it tumbles around.
Adele nervously observes how the two inside react.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Why did you up and leave when you did?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I met two... very interesting people.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: When you study volcanoes, you're always visiting new places.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I remember. You met each other in here a lot.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Mm. And if they came, you'd plug your guitar in, and off you went with your heavy metal racket.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Magna always felt 'that boy at the cafe' never seemed to welcome them too much.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Aah... I was just a little too willful of a brat, back then.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: It wasn't meant at them specifically...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I know. And they didn't take it to heart.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: You gave them coffee soda to try once, and make us swear to secrecy that we wouldn't tell Grandpa Mockingbird.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: He couldn't stand the drinks I came up with. Every time I added them to the menu, he'd wipe them off... They were just as bizarre to him as my axe, and my drumkit.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: By the way, that wasn't just your average coffee soda. It was called 'volcanic coffee.'

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Alright, alright, yes, 'volcanic coffee.'

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: It was a nice drink, in any case. After we went to Leithanien, Katia would follow your recipe to recreate the flavor for himself.

spans.text: a nice drink, in any case. After we went to Leithanien, Katia would follow your recipe to recreate the flavor for himself.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: How are... Katia, and... Magna doing?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: I remember when you left Siesta, you said, you'd be visiting every volcano across the land with them.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: I spent a long, long time with them on our travels.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: But a few years ago, we strayed apart.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Strayed?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: And we're never to meet again.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Was it...? I'm so sorry...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Hence why I came back. Opened that museum. Hoped I could preserve all the research they'd done.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: When I—saw you at the museum that day, it completely... totally blindsided me.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: It was a great surprise to me too. You're nothing like the noisy little child I remember.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: You, too... You're a museum curator and everything.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Mm. I suppose I've turned an old ideal or two into reality. No matter what, though, the conviction that keeps me going now isn't... really what drove me in the first place anymore.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Still, change isn't always a bad thing, wouldn't you say?
The two lapse into silence for a while. The customer lightly stirs at the coffee in her cup.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Did you go to the trade fair today?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: The trade fair? I did. Tourists were profuse, proprietors were in high spirits—much like the Siesta of old.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Maybe once this place is all rebuilt, and the tourist influx comes, I'll have an idea or two about what's next for me.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: For example?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Who knows...? I'll probably keep running a cafe, but maybe a rock 'n' roll cafe, or just a music shop, filled to the walls with drum kits and guitars. Lots to try. Always someone out there who'll enjoy it.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Just like you say... just like the Siesta of old.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Oh, something very funny that happened today too. I was at the trade fair, and I saw this soft drink from Columbia. The recipe was one-for-one with my 'volcanic coffee.' The exact same.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Well, I didn't leak your secret recipe!

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: No, no, it was a year ago when I was planning to shutter the shop. I told somebody else about how to make it.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: But honestly... it's just coffee plus soda water. Of course some Columbian could've come up with it on their own too.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Hand-brewed coffee and soda water. How did you come up with it at first?

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: When I was young, I thought coffee was so bitter, I was convinced I had to add something to even make it drinkable!

spans.text: When I was young, I thought coffee was so bitter, I was
I had to add something to even make it drinkable!

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: You shook the whole cafe playing your rock 'n' roll, and yet you were bad with bitter.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Who'd care about something like that, back then?
Keller laughs, downing the last gulp of coffee in her cup. The aroma lingers lazily in the cafe air.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: So, want soda in this cup too?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: But after this one, I may well genuinely spend the whole night awake.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Adele, let me just be upfront. I told them what I told them, but the lot of them are dying to go inside, probably to taste the volcanic coffee.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: To make up for the owner's losses, I can leave a product from today's trade fair in exchange!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: A product from the fair? Where'd you get it?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: A lovely little child gave me it!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Honest!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Ah! We can't go in now!

steps.name: Agitated Creature
steps.text: (Sniffs in corner)

steps.name: Dozy Creature
steps.text: (Turns over a box)
The restless lambs drag a case of glass bottles out from the junk to Adele's side, and zealously churn through it for something.
Eventually, they get a few bottles of carbonated water clamped in their mouths and pull off the metal caps, acting like they've found treasure.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What are you doing? Didn't you want to a soda?
The lambs bounce about, each one with a shiny bottle cap on their head. Then they line up together, and playfully scamper away.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: *sigh* I said to wait. What makes them even more impatient than me?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What was all that...?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Oh, that's the 'seed' they were after!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: What about these bottle caps... makes them seeds?

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: The world as they see it isn't quite the world you all see.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: This—itty-bitty little round thing—gets taken by fowlbeasts to places far far away, where it takes root and sprouts, and becomes something completely unlike before.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Some become soda caps, some become sauce lids, each one has a different flavor, but they all have their own charms.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: I assume at least one of them drank that sort of volcanic coffee in Columbia before, so this rings that bell in them particularly loud.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Isn't it more than fascinating to view the world that way?

steps.name: Left-Behind Creature
steps.text: (Digs at the soil)

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But all that granted... *sigh* Just because you planted the bottle caps doesn't mean they're going to grow into drinks.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Let them have their fun.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: The answers will grow by themselves.

steps.name: Costa
steps.text: Hello, Costa here.

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: Mr. Costa, this is your grandfather's clinician. I'm sorry to tell you this, but... your grandfather passed away this evening.

steps.name: Voice on the Phone
steps.text: I can't know if this will be any comfort to you, but I want you to know he left us peacefully.
